cases.purpose: The paginator requests page 2 at exactly the nextPageTimestamp page 1 returned (1500, no offset), stops on the terminal page, reports COMPLETE, and retrieves 4 events although two of them are identical in every observable field.

rationale.text: The paginator's three rules: the cursor is passed back VERBATIM as the next startTime because the schema documents it as exactly that; nothing is deduplicated because multiple legitimate events can share every field; there is no page-level retry.

limitations: Synthetic pages. A real report's page boundary has not been captured into the corpus.

cases.purpose: Over the second report's real context, actor 25 (the 100 % parse) and actor 8 (the 8 % parse) both resolve as Rogue/Assassination at revision 22, logVersion 17, gameVersion 1 — identically, because performance is not an identity fact. Boss 235 is SOURCE_NOT_A_PLAYER and an id no actor has is SOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

rationale.text: Identity is read from subType and friendlySpecs at the roster index and from nothing else. Two subjects at opposite ends of the same board resolve the same way, which is the point of keeping performance context off the identity path.

cases.purpose: Over the real report context, actor 19 and actor 13 resolve as Rogue/Assassination with the report revision (30), logVersion 17 and gameVersion 1; pet 29 is SOURCE_NOT_A_PLAYER; an id no actor has is SOURCE_NOT_FOUND; a player listed in master data but not in fight 7's friendlyPlayers is SOURCE_NOT_IN_FIGHT; actor -1 — which master data DOES list as an NPC — is SOURCE_NOT_FOUND because the sentinel never resolves; and asking for fight 999 when the served fight is 7 is UPSTREAM_DATA_INVALID.

rationale.text: Identity safety on real master data: class from subType, spec from friendlySpecs at the player's roster index, and every refusal explicit. The -1 entry is the interesting one — Warcraft Logs lists a boss NPC under the no-actor sentinel id, and the resolver must refuse it as not found rather than let 'the environment' become a player. The wrong-fight refusal proves the preflight trusts the fight it asked for, not the fight it was served.

limitations: A conflict between authoritative identity and OBSERVED behaviour (IDENTITY_CONFLICT) is still not captured; this pins metadata resolution only.
The redacted name `Actor19` is asserted only as the redacted form; the production identity carries whatever Warcraft Logs served.

cases.purpose: The committed A7R6 context resolves actor 7 as a Paladin whose spec at its roster index is Protection — the machine-verifiable identity M10-B's capture was planned against and re-verified live (revision 30 before and after the capture). The same report's actor 6 resolves as a Retribution Paladin, so the class alone never implies the spec; pet 37, whose petOwner is 7, is not a player.

cases.purpose: When page 2 carries data: null, the stream ends PARTIAL with MALFORMED_PAGE, the 2 events of page 1 are kept, and nothing is retried.

rationale.text: Every abnormal ending preserves what was already retrieved and records why it stopped. A failed page never becomes an empty period, which is the rule that keeps a 30-second retrieval gap from becoming 'you were idle for 30 seconds'.

cases.purpose: The parent's page 5 is removed. The paginator retrieves pages 1–4 verbatim (186 events, real cursors), requests page 5 at 2,176,396, does not receive it, and ends PARTIAL with 4 pages. The interval from 2,176,396 on is reported as NOT RETRIEVED — never as a quiet stretch of the fight.

rationale.text: Partial retrieval over REAL pages: the derivation removes one page and records it; nothing about the four retained pages changed. A 30-second retrieval gap caused by a failed page must never become 'you were idle for 30 seconds', and the only way to pin that on real data is to take a real page away and check what is reported.

limitations: The missing page is a recorded derivation; the failure class it models is a transport failure, not a specific upstream response.

cases.purpose: A ReportEventPaginator whose data is null decodes to MALFORMED_PAGINATOR. 'We could not read your events' must never become 'you produced no events'.

rationale.text: The decoder owns the classification and documents it in place: data: JSON is nullable upstream, and a null or non-array payload is a malformed page, never an empty one.

limitations: Exercises the decoder over a decoded data object, not a raw HTTP body; transport-level parsing failures are a separate boundary.

cases.purpose: Five real consecutive pages: each page's nextPageTimestamp equals the next page's first event timestamp and exceeds the previous page's last, and the paginator requests every page at exactly that cursor. The capture stopped after page 5 (cursor 2,176,472); the sixth request is answered as not retrieved, so the stream ends PARTIAL with all 5 pages / 226 events kept, in order, undeduplicated — never COMPLETE.

rationale.text: The cursor rule was documented from the schema and pinned on synthetic pages in M9-B; this case pins it on five real boundaries. The measured boundary fact — cursor = next first timestamp, strictly after the previous last — is exactly what makes passing the cursor back verbatim correct and any 'cursor + 1' or overlap-trimming heuristic wrong. The PARTIAL ending models the capture bound: a page that was never obtained is reported, not filled in.

limitations: The sixth page's absence is the capture bound, not an observed failure; UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE is the transport's classification of the executor's not-retrieved answer.

cases.purpose: One real page whose nextPageTimestamp is null: the paginator issues exactly one request and ends COMPLETE with 14 events. All 14 share timestamp 2,176,580, and all 14 are retrieved.

rationale.text: A null cursor is the only thing that ends a stream COMPLETE. This is the real terminal case the synthetic two-page sequence stood in for, and the fourteen equal timestamps are the real form of the no-deduplication rule.
